propositions: A write whose lock acquire() times out within the budget is permanently lost with no retry or spool, making the budget terminal and lossy rather than queueing.
Holder duration (not writer count) now triggers write loss: any single lock holder exceeding the 60s budget causes all waiting writers to fail regardless of service order.

Retry is implemented as bounded retry-with-backoff inside acquire() with retries parameter defaulting to 0, converting loss into latency without risking double-append since LockTimeout is raised before write body execution.

Five call sites are opted into retry via REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES env var (default 2, clamped [0,10]): three in event_append.py, one in txn.py, one in push.py; all other callers keep fail-fast via retries=0 default.

Cumulative wait time and per-pass warnings are logged on retry exhaustion; the plan-review gate itself was destroyed twice by this bug at holder durations of 88-103s, all within the planned ~181.5s retry ceiling.
